description: Discriminator: a real PreAccept message carries two commands, the first with a 70000-byte value; after marshalling, does the implementation's own decoder recover the message, or does the truncated length make it panic? Prefix: the harness builds the message and marshals it with the implementation's codec, then unmarshals from those bytes, wrapping only the decode in recover so a panic is reported instead of killing the test. Controls: the prerequisite prints the command count, the first value's size and the wire size, and the result prints whether the decoder panicked, the panic value and the bytes left.

harness.description: In-package Go test that marshals a PreAccept with an oversized first command value and decodes it with the real unmarshaller.
semantic_changes: harness-only scaffolding: no replica is constructed; the message and command codecs are called directly
the decode is wrapped in recover() to observe a panic; the replica reader in production has no recover around its unmarshal

legality.derivation: The PreAccept is the message a leader sends for a proposal and it carries its commands in exactly this array form, so the input is a real protocol message.
legality.applicability: One message, two commands, no replica.
unresolved: the reader's own path around unmarshal is not exercised, only the decode itself

grounding.derivation: The event reports whether the decoder survived the message and what it had left, which is the receiver-side consequence of the truncated length.
grounding.applicability: The message carried a value beyond the length field's range.

observable_properties.description: Decoding a message the implementation itself marshalled must not panic.

uncertainties: the harness observes the decode panic rather than the replica reader terminating; the reader has no recover around its unmarshal, so the panic is inferred to end the process
the shipped configuration's 1000-byte commands never reach the boundary
